content:
Eleven people believed to have been deprived of their liberty were freed during patrols in Nuevo Laredo, according to an account from Mexico's Army and National Guard reported by El Autómata. The intervention took place on October 22 as part of the National Public Security Strategy, the commands of the Fourth Military Region and the Eighth Military Zone said, according to the report.

The people found were given food and medical care before being transferred to the Attorney General's Office of the Republic for the corresponding ministerial proceedings, according to the report. During the operation, authorities also seized a short firearm, 15 magazines, 387 cartridges and tactical equipment, which were placed at the disposal of the ministerial authority.

The official account did not specify the exact place where the people were found, how long they had been held, or their nationalities, and it reported no arrests connected with the case, according to El Autómata. The Defense Secretariat said the actions are part of coordinated work with Tamaulipas authorities to strengthen security and protect the public, while the Attorney General's Office will continue the investigation to determine responsibility.

Sources:

  • El Autómata, "Ejército y Guardia Nacional liberan a 11 personas en Nuevo Laredo," October 28, 2026
